articles.title: McDonald's McRib Marketing Faces Scrutiny After Judge Rejects Bid To End Consumer Deception Case
articles.desc: A federal judge has allowed consumer deception, fraud and unjust enrichment claims over McDonald's McRib marketing to continue, while dismissing five other claims without prejudice.
articles.content: McDonald's McRib Marketing Faces Scrutiny After Judge Rejects Bid To End Consumer Deception Case | IBTimes UK McDonald's McRib marketing will remain under legal scrutiny after a federal judge in Chicago refused to throw out key On Friday, 30 October 2026, Judge April Perry allowed core allegations of consumer deception, fraud and unjust enrichment to proceed, while dismissing five other claims without prejudice in the proposed class action. Four consumers originally sued McDonald's in December, alleging that the McRib's name and rib-shaped patty suggest it contains pork rib meat. They say customers paid a premium for a sandwich allegedly made from less expensive cuts. McDonald's rejects the accusations and says it has been transparent about its ingredients. The ruling allows the plaintiffs to pursue their case but does not establish that the company misled customers. Nor has the court certified a class action. Judge Keeps Deception Claims Alive in McRib Row Perry ruled that it was too early to accept that reasonable customers could not expect rib meat in the McRib. She described the plaintiffs' understanding of the sandwich's name as 'not unreasonable or fanciful.' The distinction matters. At this stage, the court is assessing whether the allegations can move forward, not deciding whether consumers were actually deceived. According to Reuters, Perry also considered advertisements emphasising the patty's ridged, rib-like appearance. She said that presentation could support an allegation of intent to defraud, although the plaintiffs would need further evidence. McDonald's argued that its distinctive product names do not deceive reasonable buyers. Its lawyers maintained that preferring a particular pork cut does not transform accurate marketing into The company also pointed to descriptions on its website identifying the sandwich as pork. Perry, however, questioned whether customers should have to research ingredients before buying a $7 (approximately €6.25 and £5.23) sandwich. What does a name promise when the product underneath is deliberately shaped to match it? The case now leaves that question open for further proceedings. The decision was not an across-the-board victory for the consumers. Five claims were dismissed without prejudice, according to Fox Business, meaning the plaintiffs may seek to bring them again. The surviving claims concern consumer deception, fraud and unjust enrichment. The company describes the unusual design as 'fun,' rather than claiming the patty contains rib meat. Its published explanation says the meat is shaped using a special press similar to equipment used for hamburger patties. The sandwich is then served with barbecue sauce, onions and pickles. Producers that can keep costs down are better placed to stay cash positive, continue investing and avoid raising capital at unfavourable prices. The challenge will be sustaining that performance as the expansion moves through execution, since construction activity can sometimes disrupt existing operations. articles.title: Drivers warned over viral fuel-saving petrol pump trick that experts say won't work
articles.desc: Fuel-saving ‘slow squeeze’ hack debunked by expert, who warns UK motorists it will not cut petrol or diesel costs; repeated topping off can damage vehicles.
articles.content: Expert debunks viral fuel-saving petrol pump trick | South Wales Argus Expert debunks viral fuel-saving petrol pump trick An expert has debunked a viral hack on saving money when filling up at a petrol station This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. A motoring expert has debunked a viral fuel-saving tip making the rounds on social media. The so-called "slow squeeze" method, gaining traction on TikTok and Instagram, claims that gently squeezing the fuel pump trigger while filling up will get motorists more petrol or diesel for their money by reducing air bubbles and foam in the tank. The theory has gained attention online, with one TikTok post under the tag "Fuel Prices UK" reaching almost 250,000 views. However, Graham Conway, managing director at , said the advice is misguided and unlikely to deliver any real benefit. Mr Conway said: "The ‘slow squeeze’ hack is popular on platforms like TikTok and Instagram, but you’re highly unlikely to see any real benefit. "Modern fuel pumps have clever systems designed to prevent air or vapour from affecting the measurement of fuel that comes out of the nozzle. "You can’t somehow game the system with the trickle method. "The only thing that might happen is that you take ages to fill up, angering other drivers patiently waiting behind you." The creator of the trend argued that filling up too quickly creates bubbles in the tank, similar to pouring a fizzy drink too fast. Despite Mr Conway’s explanation, some social media users remain convinced the method works. One commenter said: "I always fill up holding the lever halfway and my petrol lasts way longer. "By holding the lever in all the way in we are paying for a lot of air too." Another claimed that it could "make a litre or two difference in a fill up." Motorists urged to avoid common mistake when filling up Mr Conway also used the opportunity to warn against another common mistake at the pump: topping off the tank after the nozzle clicks. He said: "Squeezing the fuel pump trigger after the nozzle has automatically clicked off, also known as ‘topping off,’ might seem like a sensible way to squeeze a little extra fuel into your tank. "But doing so repeatedly could actually end up damaging your car, potentially leaving you facing an expensive repair bill. "Most modern petrol cars are fitted with an evaporative emissions control system, which captures petrol vapours from the fuel tank and stores them in a charcoal canister, preventing them from escaping into the atmosphere. "However, if you continue forcing petrol into an already full tank, liquid fuel can enter parts of this system that are designed to handle vapour rather than liquid. "This can damage the charcoal canister and other components, potentially triggering an engine management warning light and even contributing to an MOT failure. "Although diesel vehicles generally don't use the same charcoal-canister system, overfilling can still cause fuel to spill or interfere with the tank's venting arrangements. "Repairs to a damaged evaporative emissions system can run into hundreds of pounds, depending on the vehicle and the extent of the damage. "So, while an occasional extra squeeze isn't guaranteed to cause problems, it's best to stop filling when the nozzle automatically clicks off. "That way, you can avoid the risk of an unnecessary repair bill." The warnings come as UK motorists continue to look for ways to cut costs at the pump amid persistently high fuel prices. Neurotech has dosed the first patient in its pivotal Beyond Harmony autism trial The US FDA has cleared an Investigational New Drug application for NTI164 Its AGM is coming up following a recent placement , a clinical-stage company developing a cannabinoid-based therapy for paediatric neurological disorders, is taking a different path from most of the medicinal cannabis sector. Rather than supplying unapproved products through special access schemes, it is running a late-stage trial of its lead candidate NTI164 in children with autism spectrum disorder, aiming for formal regulatory approval. Neurotech International remains one of the more closely followed ASX Neurotech announced that all sites had been initiated and the first patient had been dosed in its pivotal late-stage Beyond Harmony study of NTI164 in autism spectrum disorder. The trial is a multi-centre, randomised, placebo-controlled study led by Professor Michael Fahey. The company said it expects to be fully funded through to the topline data readout for the trial following completion of a recent placement. It also received funds from a loan secured against its expected research and development tax incentive. The US Food and Drug Administration cleared Neurotech's Investigational New Drug application for NTI164, which the company said supports its global development, registration and commercialisation strategy. It also received notices of allowance for US patent applications expected to protect NTI164 for many years. An IND clearance allows clinical trials in the US and is an important step toward eventual partnering or registration in the world's largest pharmaceutical market. While the trial proceeds, NTI164 is available in Australia through an Authorised Prescriber program, which has expanded to more clinical sites. This provides early access for some patients and a small amount of activity before formal approval. Regulation is reshaping the industry. After AHPRA and the TGA moved against high-volume prescribers, sales volumes fell sharply, according to newsGP, and the TGA's business plan includes options to reform the framework governing unapproved medicinal cannabis products. Only a handful of medicinal cannabis products have undergone full regulatory evaluation in Australia. A successful late-stage trial would give NTI164 a level of evidence most products in the market lack, which could become more valuable if regulators tighten access to unapproved products. , Neurotech is a drug development story rather than a cultivation or distribution business. It reported a loss for the last financial year, and its shares trade at just a few cents, well outside the for that day-to-day backdrop. Its AGM is scheduled for the coming weeks. Late-stage trials are designed to provide the evidence regulators require for approval, typically comparing a treatment against placebo in a larger patient group. A positive outcome would be a significant milestone for a cannabinoid therapy in paediatric autism, an area with limited approved treatment options. Recruitment speed is one of the biggest determinants of trial timelines, so updates on enrolment will give an early indication of when topline data might arrive. articles.title: NASA Is Offering You a Chance to Travel 1 Billion Miles to a Mysterious Moon: Here’s How to Join the Mission
articles.desc: NASA's Dragonfly mission offers the public a rare opportunity to send their names to Titan, a mysterious world that could reveal clues about life's origins.
articles.content: NASA Is Offering You a Chance to Travel 1 Billion Miles to a Mysterious Moon: Here’s How to Join the Mission NASA is inviting people around the world to send their names to Titan, Saturn’s largest moon, aboard its upcoming Dragonfly mission. The names will travel on a spacecraft designed to fly across an alien landscape, investigate organic chemistry, and search for conditions that could support life. NASA Is Opening the Door to an Extraordinary Journey , the Send Your Name to Titan campaign allows members of the public to become symbolic passengers on one of the agency’s most ambitious planetary exploration missions. Submitted names will be stored on a digital chip carried by Dragonfly, a robotic rotorcraft designed to explore Titan’s surface. will use eight rotors to travel between scientific destinations. Titan’s dense atmosphere and relatively weak gravity make powered flight particularly practical, allowing the spacecraft to cover distances that would be challenging for a ground-based vehicle. The mission will investigate a world where liquid methane and ethane form lakes and seas, while complex organic molecules accumulate across the surface. “NASA’s Dragonfly mission will simply blow your mind,” said Nicky Fox, associate administrator, Science Mission Directorate, NASA Headquarters in Washington. “By flying the first-ever rotorcraft science mission, NASA will explore Saturn’s largest moon, Titan, as we search for signs of habitability on a distant world that is most similar to our own. We are excited to bring humanity along for the journey of a lifetime, and we invite everyone to send their names on this small, but mighty rotorcraft that will unlock the secrets of the universe in what is widely considered one of the most exciting space missions of our lifetime.” Your name could fly on Saturn’s largest moon. NASA’s Dragonfly mission will launch in 2028 to explore the dunes, lakes, and rivers of Saturn’s moon, Titan, and your name can come along! Join the voyage and claim your boarding pass: https://t.co/iinCnJaqIP https://t.co/FQZvfBGUZo Why Titan Could Reveal Clues About Life Beyond Earth Titan is unlike any other moon in the solar system. Larger than Mercury, it possesses a thick, nitrogen-rich atmosphere, weather systems, and surface liquids. Yet its environment is radically different from Earth’s: surface temperatures hover around minus 290 degrees Fahrenheit (minus 179 degrees Celsius) . At these temperatures, water ice behaves like rock, while methane participates in a cycle resembling Earth’s water cycle, forming clouds, rain, rivers, and lakes. Scientists are particularly interested in Titan because its atmosphere produces complex carbon-based compounds. These materials may help researchers understand the chemical processes that preceded the emergence of life on early Earth. Dragonfly will examine surface materials using scientific instruments capable of analyzing their chemical composition. Its measurements will help determine how far prebiotic chemistry can progress under Titan’s unusual conditions. The mission is not designed to establish that life exists on Titan. Instead, it will investigate whether the moon possesses, or once possessed, environments favorable to biological processes. A Flying Laboratory Will Explore Places No Rover Has Reached Dragonfly represents a different approach to robotic exploration. Rather than remaining at one landing site, the spacecraft will conduct repeated flights, collecting measurements from locations separated by kilometers. Its planned exploration region includes Titan’s equatorial dunes and areas associated with the Selk impact crater, where scientists suspect past interactions between liquid water and organic materials may have created environments suitable for complex chemistry. articles.title: ‘Maps have changed as their purpose has changed’
articles.desc: Explore how cartography evolved over seven centuries, shifting motives from pilgrimage routes to global trade and digital maps.
articles.content: ‘Maps have changed as their purpose has changed’ - The Hindu Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription ‘Maps have changed as their purpose has changed’ - October 31, 2026 09:14 pm IST - HYDERABAD Map collector and curator Prshant Lahoti showing one of the earliest maps used by pilgrims in India. | Photo Credit: ARRANGEMENT It was sweeping history of seven centuries of cartography packed into 35 minutes at the Kalakriti Art Gallery here on Saturday (October 31). Map collector and curator Prshant Lahoti dove into his massive collection of maps and drawing that date from earliest Indian maps that showed the path for pilgrims to the current day Google maps that are available at the click of a button. He began with the earliest conception of Indian cosmography where the world was believed to be a circular island or Jambudvipa to a map that showed he passage for a pilgrim from Haridwar to reach the temple of Badrinath. “The maps have changed over a period of time as the purpose of the maps changed. Maps were not how the world was but how the mapmaker believed or thought it was,” said Mr. Lahoti at his talk on ‘Mapping Memory’ which is part of the Hyderabad Art Week. “Printing technology changed map making and its purpose as well. The Ptolemy world map is based on the descriptions of various places by the historian in his book on Geography. Neither the map makers travelled nor did Ptolemy and it was a collection of information,” he said. “The Portuguese mapped the world and kept it a secret till a Dutch trader and spy Jan Huygen van Linschoten collected the information from the Portuguese and wrote a tell-all book that changed the trade history of the world. Trade was driving geography. The cartographers never came to India but collected information from travellers and used their imagination,” Mr Lahoti said showing a world map that did not look anything like what we know now. articles.title: Google's AI satellite sends a very expensive haiku to Earth
articles.desc: Experimental orbital datacenter prototype puts its TPU to work producing poetry
articles.content: Google's AI satellite sends a very expensive haiku to Earth Google's AI satellite sends a very expensive haiku to Earth Experimental orbital datacenter prototype puts its TPU to work producing poetry Backbone of a beast – charting Nvidia's rise to networking titan Voyager 1 gives controllers the silent treatment NASA ponders a Hubble servicing mission or a controlled deorbit Google's search revenue Ferrari hits an AI-powered speed bump GSA left sensitive Google Drive files open to staff, contractors Google on Friday celebrated receiving a poem from its first experimental orbital AI datacenter satellite. and put into low Earth orbit, has responded to a ground station prompt to "Write a haiku from the perspective of a TPU orbiting Earth, with the wonderful world spinning beneath you." Travis Beals, senior director of Google's interdisciplinary research team, said that with Suncatcher's host and TPU trays powered up and machine learning tests completed, the onboard Gemma 4 model achieved its "Hello World" milestone by sending an inference response from orbit. "During a ground-station pass, we uplinked our first prompt to our onboard Gemma 4 open model, asking it to generate a haiku about being in space," wrote Beals in a And as the satellite passed over Svalbard, Norway, the orbiting AI model responded over the downlink: Those roughly 20 tokens would cost about $0.000012 if generated through the Google Cloud API, based on Gemma 4 26B's of $0.15 per million input tokens and $0.60 per million output tokens, excluding input costs. Add in a satellite weighing perhaps 500 kg, based on the mass of SpaceX's Starlink satellites, and a retail launch price of around $7,000 per kg, and you have a very expensive haiku. , if the cost of getting a satellite into low Earth orbit can be brought down to $200/kg, the launch cost amortized over the satellite's useful life (~$810–7,500/kW/year) could be comparable to current electricity spending for terrestrial datacenters in the US (~$570–3,000/kW/year). Google predicts that SpaceX could achieve that by 2035, more or less, and considers it strategically beneficial to prototype well in advance of that actually happening. After the haiku, Beals said, "we tested space-themed limericks and telemetry prompts reporting the technical status of the payload systems." Next up: tests for evaluating how TPUs perform under thermal stress and radiation. Google has already done some laboratory testing of its Trillium Cloud TPU and AMD host server to see how well they can withstand a 67 MeV proton beam. The system's high-bandwidth memory shows the most sensitivity in terms of the total ionizing dose – it exhibits irregularities after a cumulative dose of 2 krad(Si), which is about 3× Google's minimum requirement for TID survival of 750 rad(Si). "For typical transformer workloads, the observed SDC [silent data corruption] rate of approximately one event/17 rad, at an estimated orbital dose of 150 rad(Si)/year, translates to a very low failure probability on the order of 1 per 3 million inferences, assuming 1 inference per second," Google researchers said in "While this error rate is likely acceptable for inference, the impact of SEEs on training jobs, and the efficacy of system-level mitigations, requires further study." Indeed, the study will continue. Next year, the plan is to test a pair of interconnected satellites. Rather than lofting large satellites into orbit, Google anticipates sending a constellation of many smaller satellites that communicate with one another. ® Google's AI satellite sends a very expensive haiku to Earth Experimental orbital datacenter prototype puts its TPU to work producing poetry Goth aesthetic gone wild: a user's self-inflicted black screen of non-death in Windows 3.1’s Labeled in black on black - controls for a galactic hyper-hearse or ill-advised Windows theme? articles.title: Five ways to unlock better herd management decisions
articles.desc: Realizing the potential of your herd management system may not require a new investment — just a closer look at the tools and workflows already in place.
articles.content: Five ways to unlock better herd management decisions – AgriNews Five ways to unlock better herd management decisions LAWTON, Okla. — Herd management software supports nearly every decision and workflow across a dairy. But even the most capable system only delivers value when accurate information is entered consistently and on time. “You can have the best protocols, the most advanced technologies and the best team, but unless those pieces are connected through timely, accurate data entry, it is difficult to track the impact of the work happening on your farm,” said Rosa DePriest, VAS dairy support team lead. Capturing more value from your herd management system does not necessarily require another tool. Often, it starts with better use of the capabilities already available and aligning them with daily workflows. The good news? Small changes can have a big impact. Here are five ways to strengthen your herd management workflows. Animal care understandably takes priority over sitting down at a computer. Problems can arise, however, when information is written on a paper list, calf card or loose note to be entered later. Sometimes that information isn’t entered into the system right away. Other times, it never makes it in at all. “The goal is to make doing the task and recording the task one process,” DePriest said. “We want to eliminate that second job of going back later and entering everything again.” Mobile tools can allow employees to view information and record events while working with the animal. At Your Legacy Genetics near Tulare in central California, Derrick Nunes and his team use handheld scanners and their herd management mobile app to streamline genomic sampling. “We scan the EID and the sample barcode or QR code, and it is immediately assigned to the right animal in Pocket CowCard,” he said. “Eliminating manual entry has significantly improved our data accuracy and efficiency.” Even farms that aren’t ready for mobile entry can still use batch or bulk entry and more structured paper workflows to reduce repetitive work and improve accuracy. Some managers hesitate to expand mobile data access because they are concerned that incorrect information may be entered. DePriest said access controls, training and accountability can help. Individuals who only need to see cow information can receive view-only access, while veterinarians or other consultants could have access to analyze data without changing the underlying records. Farms generally find success with one of two approaches: train multiple employees to enter information as they complete their work or designate one person or group of people to collect, verify and enter data. “Someone on the farm ultimately must be accountable for the data,” DePriest said. “That person makes sure the information gets entered and stays up to date.” Regular training is equally important, especially as employee roles change. “We train employees on animal care, safety and other important areas,” DePriest said. “Data stewardship should be part of that conversation too — how to enter information and why it matters.” Nunes said their herd management app’s ease of use helped his team adopt the technology. “We have about 10 people who can use it and every one of them picked it up quickly,” he said. “That low learning curve made the rollout painless.” One of the simplest ways to improve efficiency is to reduce the number of times employees need to locate or handle the same animals. Merging work lists and utilizing mobile tools allow teams to complete vet checks, vaccinations and other scheduled work in the same pass. “If two teams are going through the same pen for different reasons, can we combine those work lists?” DePriest asked. “Fewer trips through pens can mean fewer labor hours, less time away from feed or stalls and fewer touches on the animals.” One dairy moved from paper lists to RFID-enabled mobile workflows, cutting a two-day, multi-site vet check process to one day and saving an esti

articles.desc: Nasdaq suffers worst month since March 2025 as technology stocks tumble Bitcoin tests key support as Binance security fears weigh Week ahead: Elections, rate decisions and jobs take center stage Earnings next week: Can Apple, Palantir and AMD restore confidence? articles.content: Nasdaq suffers worst month since March 2025 as technology stocks tumble Bitcoin tests key support as Binance security fears weigh Week ahead: Elections, rate decisions and jobs take center stage Earnings next week: Can Apple, Palantir and AMD restore confidence? Fed’s Logan: At least two more quarter-point rate hikes needed Carney: Canada, EU working toward deepest possible partnership, short of accession Fed’s Daly: AI matters for near- and medium-term policy Fitch on UK Budget: Policy continuity leaves a tough delivery challenge Fed's Barkin: Direction of travel is straightforward for the Fed Canada GDP for August 0.0% vs 0.2% estimate US employment cost index for Q3 +0.8% vs +0.8% expected Morning Kickstart: Tech hammered as Amazon and Intel tumble; oil rises despite peace talk investingLive European session wrap: AI spending fears spook tech stocks; dollar falls alongside yields, gold October ended with investors taking a harder look at the cost of the AI boom. Technology led a broad stock-market decline as disappointing reactions to Amazon and Intel earnings reinforced concerns about spending, profitability and cash flow. Strong demand remains part of the story, but investors are becoming more demanding about when that demand translates into returns. The cross-market moves were revealing. Treasury yields declined even as several Fed officials argued for further tightening. Oil moved higher, keeping inflation concerns alive, while gold failed to benefit from lower yields. Bonds attracted defensive demand, but the protection did not extend across every traditional haven. Dollar finishes mixed after recovering earlier losses The dollar was mixed in the supplied late-session snapshot. Its strongest performance was against the euro, with EURUSD down 0.13% at 1.1164. Its weakest performance was against sterling, with GBPUSD up 0.11% at 1.3390. USDJPY slipped 0.06% to 157.59, while USDCHF rose 0.05% to 0.8246. USDCAD edged down 0.06% to 1.3979 despite disappointing Canadian growth data. AUDUSD gained 0.07% to 0.7032, while NZDUSD fell 0.07% to 0.5629. The mixed finish marked a recovery from the dollar’s broader weakness earlier in the session. Falling U.S. yields provided a headwind, but the currency market did not deliver a uniform risk-off response. Treasury yields fall despite calls for more tightening Treasury yields were lower across the curve in the supplied snapshot. The 2-year yield fell 6.43 basis points to 4.5917%, the 5-year declined 7.87 basis points to 4.7233%, the 10-year dropped 5.86 basis points to 4.9303%, and the 30-year eased 1.76 basis points to 5.3114%. The larger declines in shorter and intermediate maturities steepened the curve. The move was consistent with defensive demand as stocks weakened, even though the Fed commentary offered little reassurance that the tightening cycle was finished. Lower yields alone were insufficient to offset the concerns facing technology shares. U.S. stocks: Nasdaq leads the retreat The supplied end-of-day index readings showed: Dow industrial average: −573.08 points, or −1.09%, at 51,775.17. S&P 500: −140.32 points, or −1.82%, at 7,580.07. Nasdaq Composite: −747.73 points, or −2.86%, at 25,437.00. Russell 2000: −47.37 points, or −1.66%, at 2,811.84. Nasdaq 100: −1,017.66 points, or −3.46%, at 28,384.85. The selling extended beyond technology, but the Nasdaq indices carried the heaviest burden. The Dow held up better on a relative basis, although a decline of more than 570 points still reflected a difficult session. AI faces questions about financing and returns Amazon and Intel remained central to the earnings concerns. Investors questioned how much spending would be required to sustain AI growth and how quickly that investment would produce stronger profits and cash flow. A separate Financial Times report covered by InvestingLive added a financing concern: Blackstone reportedly told Anthropic that it might not obtain an investment-grade credit rating after its IPO. This was a reported possibility, rather than a ratings decision, but it sharpened the focus on borrowing costs. Intel was down more than 30% in that afternoon report, with substantial losses across chip and infrastructure suppliers including AMD, Arm, Marvell, Astera Labs and Coherent. Those were intraday readings. European stocks mostly lower European markets also finished mostly lower, with the UK holding a modest gain: Germany’s DAX: −221.47 points, or −0.85%, at 25,818.22. France’s CAC 40: −0.58 points, or −0.01%, at 7,969.43. UK’s FTSE 100: +7.73 points, or +0.07%, at 10,729.79. Spain’s IBEX: −204.70 points, or −1.09%, at 18,652.90. Italy’s FTSE MIB: −501.39 points, or −1.02%, at 49,290.91. Fed speak: More tightening remains on the table Today’s Fed commentary carried a predominantly hawkish message, although the speakers differed in how directly they addressed the next policy move. Barkin favored gradual adjustment, Musalem argued for another increase soon, and Logan outlined a minimum of two additional quarter-point hikes. Daly concentrated on AI’s implications for the Fed’s inflation and employment objectives. Richmond Fed President Barkin described the direction of policy as straightforward, with the pace still open to debate. He favored a gradual approach but pointed to resilient consumer spending, broad business cost pressures and companies preparing to pass those costs to customers. His comments on AI were particularly relevant to the day’s market debate: the investment surge is adding demand and straining supply chains, creating inflation pressures that monetary policy can lean against. His assessment suggested that economic resilience continues to give the Fed room to address persistent inflation. San Francisco Fed President Daly focused on how AI affects both price stability and employment. She emphasized that those effects matter for policy in the near and medium term. Her remarks did not establish a preference for a hike or a pause. The takeaway was that AI’s effects on the economy are already relevant to current monetary policy decisions. St. Louis Fed President Musalem delivered a more explicit call for action, saying rates would need to rise again soon. He viewed monetary policy and overall financial conditions as accommodative, with inflation unlikely to ease sufficiently without additional Fed action. Higher bond yields had tightened conditions, but not enough in his assessment. His preference was to act earlier in smaller increments, reducing the risk that delayed action eventually requires a sharper adjustment. A strong economy and labor market supported that approach, while inflation risks remained tilted higher. Dallas Fed President Logan was the most specific about the amount of tightening she considered necessary. She called for at least two more quarter-point increases to make policy modestly restrictive, followed by a pause to assess whether further action was needed. Skipping a meeting, in her view, would not change the destination. Gradual adjustments could help households, businesses and investors adapt, but she regarded the lack of progress toward the 2% inflation target as unacceptable. Her message made clear that a pause should not automatically be interpreted as the end of tightening. For traders, the distinction matters: Treasury yields fell on the day, but these remarks did not amount to a dovish shift from the Fed. Economic data: Labor costs moderate, growth signals soften The U.S. Employment Cost Index rose 0.8% in the third quarter, matching expectations and slowing from 0.9%. Wage growth eased to 0.7% from 0.9%, while benefit costs increased 0.9%, down from 1.0%. The report offered some reassurance on compensation pressures, although it did not resolve the broader inflation concerns raised by Fed officials. Chicago PMI fell to 55.3, below the 56.1 estimate and down from 58.8. Activity remained above the 50 dividing line, but the pace of expansion slowed. Canada’s August GDP was unchanged versus expectations for 0.2% growth. The advance estimate pointed to a 0.1% decline in September, reinforcing the picture of an economy struggling to build momentum. German preliminary inflation also came in softer than expected. Annual CPI and harmonized inflation both slowed to 2.8%, below forecasts of 3.0% and 3.1%, respectively. Oil rises as Middle East risks persist WTI crude traded at $102.89, up $0.89 or 0.87% in the supplied snapshot. InvestingLive’s oil coverage highlighted Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and reports of U.S. preparations for potential strikes on Iran. Those developments kept supply risks in focus heading into the weekend. Elevated energy prices also complicated the inflation outlook, even as Treasury yields declined. Gold and silver join the selling Spot gold fell approximately $146.24, or 3.64%, to $3,874.33. Silver dropped $3.0644, or 5.88%, to $49.0756. Copper also declined 1.75% to $6.4870. Gold’s weakness stood out because Treasury yields were lower. That would normally provide support, but sellers retained control. InvestingLive’s gold analysis identified liquidation pressure associated with equity losses as a possible explanation: investors needing cash can sell liquid holdings such as gold to meet obligations elsewhere. That remains an interpretation of the selling, rather than a confirmed explanation for every transaction. Silver’s larger percentage decline, alongside weaker copper, also left the more industrially sensitive metals under pressure. Bitcoin remains under pressure Bitcoin traded at $76,803, down $989 or 1.27% in the supplied snapshot. The broader retreat from risk assets was compounded by concerns surrounding the reported Binance security breach. InvestingLive’s crypto coverage described exchange-security anxiety and leveraged liquidations as additional sources of pressure. Falling Treasury yields offered little relief as investors weighed both market-wide weakness and crypto-specific uncertainty. Next week: U.S. elections, jobs and central-bank decisions The November 2–6 calendar brings several important tests for markets, led by Tuesday’s U.S. midterm elections and Friday’s employment report. The results will help shape expectations for government policy, economic growth and the Fed’s next move. Monday starts with the U.S. ISM manufacturing report at 10:00 AM ET. Wednesday brings ADP employment at 8:15 AM ET and ISM services at 10:00 AM ET. Beyond the headline readings, traders will watch the employment and prices components for evidence of whether activity is slowing while inflation pressures persist. Tuesday’s midterm elections will determine control of the House and Senate, with implications for taxes, spending, regulation and the administration’s legislative agenda. The September JOLTS report, due at 10:00 AM ET, provides another measure of labor demand ahead of payrolls. Central banks also remain in focus. The Reserve Bank of Australia announces its decision Tuesday, November 3, Australian time—Monday evening in the U.S.—with several major banks expecting a 25-basis-point hike to 4.85%. The Bank of England follows Thursday with its rate decision and updated economic forecasts. Both events will test how policymakers balance inflation risks against the effects of tighter policy. Thursday brings U.S. jobless claims and preliminary third-quarter productivity and labor costs at 8:30 AM ET. Friday is the main economic event: U.S. payrolls, unemployment and average hourly earnings at 8:30 AM ET, alongside Canada’s employment report. Preliminary University of Michigan consumer sentiment follows at 10:00 AM ET, with inflation expectations another important barometer. Together, the reports will help determine whether the economy remains resilient enough to support further Fed tightening. What traders carry forward The next session begins with three connected questions: can technology shares stabilize, can Middle East risks ease enough to take pressure off oil, and will incoming data justify the additional tightening several Fed officials favor? Friday showed that lower Treasury yields alone are not enough to restore confidence when earnings, financing costs and inflation remain in question. This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.
